title: Adaptive cost allocation with request-lineage and harmonized ACK windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see edge cases where at-least-once request delivery and network/timeouts cause duplicated billed usage. Existing solutions (opaque replay tokens, client seals) reduce some classes of duplicates but do not handle: (1) partial success across sharded backends where some components commit and others retry, (2) long-tail retries from flaky mobile clients that re-send requests with different client-generated IDs, and (3) backlog-driven replays where retries overlap with late acknowledgements.

Proposal: Implement a request-lineage based accounting layer and harmonized ACK windows that allow adaptive cost allocation instead of binary charge/no-charge decisions. Key concepts: request-lineage (a server-assigned lineage_id attached to first ingest that follows the request through sharded services), harmonized ACK windows (coordinated short-lived lease/ack windows across ingestion and billing subsystems to determine final commitment), and adaptive allocation rules (fractional crediting when partial work is committed by different replicas). This reduces double billing while preserving availability and low-latency for the common case.

Goals: prevent duplicate charges for common retry patterns, enable clear reconciliation for partial/overlap cases, provide visibility for disputed charges, and keep P99 latency overhead for ingest < 10ms.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate billing in 99.95% of synthetic retry scenarios that include client replays, partial shard commits, and late acks (simulated workload documented in test-plan).
System can reconcile ambiguous/partial commits with a deterministic allocation algorithm and produce an audit trail suitable for customer support disputes.
End-to-end P99 ingest latency increase <= 10ms for steady-state traffic when lineage metadata is enabled.
Monitoring dashboards show lineage mismatch rates, harmonized ACK miss-rate, and daily duplicate-charge incidents (target < 1 per million requests).
Fallback path exists to original billing semantics (pre-lineage) via feature flag for emergency rollback.
design_notes:
Architecture: 1) Ingest API assigns an immutable lineage_id for the first canonical ingest attempt when client_id is absent or untrusted. 2) Downstream services attach their local shard_commit markers to the lineage and emit provisional commit events to the Billing Kafka topic. 3) An AckCoordinator service listens for provisional commits and harmonizes them in a configurable ACK window (default 2s) to produce final commit decisions. 4) Reconciliation worker applies adaptive allocation rules and writes finalized usage events to the consumption ledger.

Data model: add `lineage_id` (uuid) indexed on ingestion_events table; add `provisional_commits` table with expiry TTL; consumption_ledger receives `final_commit_id` with allocation fractions.

Trade-offs: extra storage for provisional commits and more events increases cost but reduces costly duplicate refunds. ACK window size balances latency vs reconciliation accuracy. We'll run experiments to pick defaults.

Alternatives considered: client-signed certificates (high client churn), fully centralized locking (scales poorly), and probabilistic dedupe with bloom filters (insufficient for partial commits).
implementation_steps: API: modify ingest endpoint to generate lineage_id when necessary and return lineage hints to clients
DB: add lineage_id to ingestion_events; create provisional_commits table with TTL and indexing
Billing pipeline: emit provisional_commit events from sharded services; update billing-kafka schema version
Service: build AckCoordinator service to collect provisional commits and produce final_commit events after ACK window
Reconciliation: implement allocation algorithm and write final events into consumption_ledger
Feature flags: gate lineage and ACK windows per-customer and per-route
Observability: add lineage mismatch metrics, duplication-rate alert, and reconciliation traces
Docs: internal runbook for disputed charges and customer-facing KB entry
test_plan: Unit tests for lineage assignment and provisional_commit lifecycle. Integration tests simulate sharded partial commits and client retries across a range of delays. End-to-end load test with 100k RPS synthetic harness: measure duplicate-charge count pre/post feature. Chaos tests: drop provisional_commit messages and verify reconciliation and fallbacks. Billing QA: run sample customers through sandbox and validate ledger against ground truth. Post-launch 48h monitor with automated rollback script if duplicate-charge incidents exceed threshold.
updates: 2026-03-11: Spike completed to evaluate ack-window latency impact; measured +6ms median overhead on a small cluster (Jonah).
